principles: Experience memory is reusable context, not authority evidence.
Keep first version transparent, file-backed, and inspectable by any agent.
Prefer prompt-only/dry-run wrappers over automatically launching external agents.
Story-scoped lessons are candidates with source references; exported memory is the reusable copy.
Every command must have deterministic CLI behavior that can be tested without a real Claude/Codex/Gemini binary.
drivers: Users lose practical agent workflow lessons when ordinary non-Koala sessions end.
Koala must not confuse experience memory with signed evidence or DONE gates.
The implementation must fit existing CLI registry, command policy, and worktree story flow.

options.name: koala-native-dev-memory-cli
pros: Shares existing CLI registry, schemas, policies, and tests
Can detect active Koala stories and write story-scoped candidates safely
Works inside project and non-story project contexts
cons: Adds several commands to Koala core
Needs careful docs to avoid evidence/gate confusion

options.name: standalone-shell-scripts
pros: Fast to create and independent from Koala lifecycle
Could be copied across repositories easily
cons: Likely to drift from Koala command policy and validation

options.name: koala-story-only-experience
pros: Simple relation to summary and delivery evidence
cons: Does not help users who explicitly are not using Koala
Next normal programming session would still miss the lessons

rationale: Implement dev-memory as native Koala CLI commands because it can serve ordinary non-story programming while still linking candidates back to active stories without treating memory as gate evidence.

preMortem.scenario: Experience memory accidentally becomes accepted as DONE evidence.
preMortem.trigger: DONE or delivery code treats experience-candidates.json as a signed artifact.
preMortem.consequence: Agents could pass gates with narrative memory instead of verification evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Docs and tests assert candidates are non-authoritative and command policy keeps dev-memory separate from gate evidence.

preMortem.scenario: Preflight output becomes noisy and users stop reading it.
preMortem.trigger: Search returns long unrelated history or transcript bodies.
preMortem.consequence: The feature recreates context overload instead of preventing repeated mistakes.
preMortem.mitigation: Default preflight cap is five entries and sixty lines, with summaries/reuse prompts only.

preMortem.scenario: Duplicate capture creates an unmaintainable memory pile.
preMortem.trigger: Repeated finish/capture stores the same Claude CLI stalled lesson with slightly different words.
preMortem.consequence: Search quality drops and agents receive contradictory context.
preMortem.mitigation: Use warn-and-link dedupe with relatedEntryIds and visible duplicate warning.

preMortem.scenario: Agent wrappers bypass Koala story flow.
preMortem.trigger: dev-start launches Claude directly inside an active story without reminding about story ownership and Koala gates.
preMortem.consequence: Implementation can skip story evidence, reviewers, or scope flow.
preMortem.mitigation: Wrappers are prompt-only by default and explicitly state active story detection and Koala flow remain authoritative.
